subject: Cognitive Science
title: Infant Perception
description: A short lesson to help you apply Infant Perception.

hook.text: Newborns see a blurry world, only about 30 centimeters deep. Just far enough for Mom's face.

buildup.text: William James called the infant's world a "blooming, buzzing confusion." He was wrong.

discovery.text: Even hours-old babies prefer faces over scrambled patterns. They arrive wired for social input.

twist.text: Newborns can distinguish their mother's voice from a stranger's. They learned it in the womb.

climax.text: Far from helpless, infants come equipped with a starter kit for making sense of the world.

punchline.text: Babies aren't blank slates. They're ready.

quiz.question: What can newborns already do at birth?
options: Prefer face-like patterns over random ones
